Daily force-of-infection offset

Source: R/foi.R
force_of_infection.Rd

Computes the infectious pressure \(\bar I(t, a)\) on each study day for each age group, used as an offset in the VE model.

Usage

force_of_infection(
  prevalence,
  pop_size,
  contact_matrix = surviver::polymod_nl,
  theta = 0,
  age_structured = TRUE,
  lag = 1L,
  study_end = max(prevalence$day),
  floor = 1e-10
)

Arguments

prevalence

Output of daily_prevalence().

pop_size

Named vector of population size by age group, e.g. from age_group_sizes().

contact_matrix

Square matrix of contacts with rows and columns in the order of names(pop_size); contact_matrix[a', a] is the mean daily contacts a person in a' has with group a. Ignored when age_structured = FALSE.

theta

Relative reduction in infectiousness of vaccinated cases (0 = as infectious as unvaccinated, 1 = not infectious). The HERMES simulations assume vaccination does not affect infectiousness, i.e. theta = 0.

age_structured

Use the contact matrix (TRUE) or overall prevalence (FALSE).

lag

Days between prevalence and the infections it causes.

study_end

Last day to compute; defaults to the last prevalence day.

floor

Lower bound applied so the log offset is finite.

Value

A tibble with day (1 to study_end), age_group and Ibar.

Details

With age structure, for recipient age group \(a\) on day \(t\): $$\bar I(t, a) = \sum_{a'} \frac{C_{a'a}}{N_a} I^{\mathrm{eff}}_{a'}(t - \ell)$$ where \(I^{\mathrm{eff}}_{a'} = I^u_{a'} + (1 - \theta) I^v_{a'}\) is the number infectious in group \(a'\) (unvaccinated plus vaccinated, the latter down-weighted by \(\theta\)) and \(\ell\) is lag.

Without age structure every group gets \(\bar I(t) = \sum_{a'} I^{\mathrm{eff}}_{a'}(t - \ell) / N\).
